paper.title: Adaptive Exploration in Linear Contextual Bandit

settings.name_in_paper: stochastic K-armed contextual linear bandit with M discrete contexts
unmapped: Finite number M of discrete contexts drawn i.i.d. from an unknown distribution p, each with positive probability
Each context m has a known action set A^m of size K that spans R^d
Standard Gaussian noise (unit variance); paper notes conditional sub-Gaussian suffices for the upper bound
settings.definition_quote: We consider the stochastic $K$-armed contextual linear bandit with a horizon of $n$ rounds and $M$ possible contexts. ... For each context $m \in [M]$ there is a known feature/action set $\cA^m\subset \mathbb R^d$ with $|\cA^m| = K$. ... First the environment samples a sequence of independent contexts $(c_t)_{t=1}^n$ from an unknown distribution $p$ over $[M]$ and each context is assumed to appear with positive probability. ... $Y_t = \langle X_t,\theta \rangle + \eta_t$, where $(\eta_t)_{t=1}^n$ is a sequence of independent standard Gaussian random variables

symbols.C_theta: optimal value of the allocation optimisation problem: inf over alpha_{x,m} >= 0 of sum alpha_{x,m} Delta_x^m s.t. ||x||^2_{(sum alpha xx^T)^{-1}} <= (Delta_x^m)^2/2 for each suboptimal x

extra_assumptions: optimal arm x_m^* unique for each context

source.label: thm:lower_bound
source.quote: Under the same conditions as \cref{lemma:confidence_width}, \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{R_{\theta}^{\pi}(n)}{\log(n)}\geq \cC(\theta,\cA^1,\ldots, \cA^M), where $\cC$ is defined as the optimal value of the following optimisation problem: \inf_{\alpha_{x,m}\in[0, \infty]}\sum_{m=1}^M\sum_{x\in\cA^m}\alpha_{x,m}\Delta_x^m subject to ... x^{\top}(\sum\alpha_{x,m}xx^{\top})^{-1}x \leq \frac{(\Delta_x^m)^2}{2}

results.notes: Expression encodes liminf R(n)/log(n) >= C_theta. Proof omitted in paper (follows Lattimore & Szepesvari 2017). Paper notes it can also be derived from Ok et al. 2018.

symbols.C_theta: optimal value of the allocation optimisation problem defined in Theorem 1

extra_assumptions: T_x^m(Delta) uniquely defined and continuous at true Delta for all contexts and actions

source.label: thm:upper_bound
source.quote: Suppose that $T_x^m(\Delta)$ is uniquely defined and $T_x^m(\cdot)$ is continuous at $\Delta$ for all contexts $m$ and actions $x \in \cA^m$. Then the policy $\pi_{\text{oam}}$ proposed in Algorithm \ref{alg:main} with $\epsilon_t = 1/\log(\log(t))$ satisfies \limsup_{n\to \infty}\frac{R_{\theta}^{\pi_{\text{oam}}}(n)}{\log (n)}\leq \cC(\theta, \cA^1,\ldots, \cA^M).

results.notes: Expression encodes limsup R(n)/log(n) <= C_theta; matches lower bound. Algorithm uses f_n depending on horizon n, so horizon known. Compute: solves a convex program per (lazy) update via CVXPY; paper calls it computationally efficient. Theorem numbering by order of appearance (thm:ucb precedes it); printed number uncertain.

bound.regime: optimal arms {x_1^*,...,x_M^*} span R^d; n -> infinity

extra_assumptions: beta_t = O(d log t) suitably chosen

source.label: thm:ucb
source.quote: Consider the policy $\pi$ that plays optimistically by X_t = \argmax_{x \in \cA^{c_t}} \ip{\hat \theta_{t-1}, x} + \|x\|_{G_t^{-1}} \beta_t^{1/2}. Suppose that $\theta$ is such that $\{x_1^*, \ldots, x_M^*\}$ spans $\mathbb R^d$. Then, for suitable $(\beta_t)_{t=1}^n$ with $\beta_t = O(d \log(t))$, it holds that $\limsup_{n\to\infty} R_\theta^\pi(n) < \infty$.

results.notes: Bounded (finite limsup) regret; constant unspecified. Encoded as O(1). Printed theorem number may differ (appears before the OAM upper bound theorem).

cited_results.setting_description: Classical K-armed Gaussian bandit (special case M=1, standard basis actions) asymptotic lower bound for consistent policies
